components.description: Native progress semantics for evidence coverage and campaign movement.
components.css: .ds-progress-label { display: grid; grid-template-columns: 1fr auto; gap: 8px 12px; color: oklch(0.53 0.035 257); font: 400 12px 'Manrope Variable', 'Avenir Next', sans-serif; } .ds-progress-label strong { color: oklch(0.25 0.045 257); font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums; } .ds-progress { grid-column: 1 / -1; width: 100%; height: 5px; appearance: none; overflow: hidden; border: 0; border-radius: 999px; background: oklch(0.95 0.035 250); } .ds-progress::-webkit-progress-bar { background: oklch(0.95 0.035 250); } .ds-progress::-webkit-progress-value { border-radius: inherit; background: oklch(0.58 0.2 258); } .ds-progress::-moz-progress-bar { border-radius: inherit; background: oklch(0.58 0.2 258); }

narrative.overview:
LeadGen's authenticated application is a bright, evidence-led workspace for sustained campaign monitoring. Ice-white canvas, deep navy navigation, white operational surfaces, and precise blue-gray rules make campaign movement legible without turning the product into a generic grid of equal-weight metrics. The design should feel like an observatory: one active process dominates, while validation, evidence quality, and the campaign ledger support it.

Authentication is a separate, scoped visual world. It retains the dark, atmospheric evidence-desk treatment and its pink signal color; those choices must not leak into the authenticated application. Across both worlds, the voice remains direct, analytical, and honest about confidence.
keyCharacteristics: Campaign movement is the dominant object in authenticated views.
White operational planes sit on an ice-blue field beside a deep navy workspace rail.
Cobalt communicates selection, active discovery, and progress; green appears only after qualification or completion.
Fine rules, restrained ambient shadow, and tabular numerals support scanning without decorative noise.
Illustrative data and planned behavior are disclosed in place rather than presented as live product capability.

rules.name: The Semantic Signal Rule
rules.body: Blue means active or progressing, green means genuinely qualified or completed, and red means failure or retry. Purple is excluded from the application status system.

rules.name: The Scoped Worlds Rule
rules.body: Dark ink, warm paper, and pink signal belong to authentication; the authenticated shell uses the daylight palette.

rules.name: The Numeric Scan Rule
rules.body: Counts, percentages, and campaign measures use tabular numerals so columns and changing values remain stable.

rules.name: The Observatory Rule
rules.body: The current campaign's movement owns the first working viewport; validation and evidence remain visibly secondary.

rules.name: The Quiet Depth Rule
rules.body: Resting operational surfaces read through tone and rules first; shadow supports the hierarchy but never replaces it.

rules.name: The Pill Restraint Rule
rules.body: Use full pills only for compact status, badge, and progress information—not for ordinary containers or primary layout.

dos: Do make campaign movement the dominant object and keep validation or evidence health in a supporting rail.
Do label illustrative campaign data clearly and disclose planned controls in the interface.
Do preserve public-evidence language and use direct terms such as ‘candidate,’ ‘qualified lead,’ ‘signal,’ and ‘evidence.’
Do use semantic markup for current navigation, current stages, tables, and progress values.
Do preserve the vertical mobile pipeline and complete stacked campaign records.
donts: Don't build a generic dashboard from equal-weight metric cards.
Don't use green for discovery, selection, or partial progress.
Don't introduce purple into application status or progress states.
Don't carry authentication's pink signal or near-black canvas into the authenticated workspace.
Don't make planned creation, search, archive, or campaign-detail behavior appear available before it is implemented.
